source_metadata.title: Updated Overall Survival Analysis From IMpower110: Atezolizumab Versus Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in Treatment-Naive Programmed Death-Ligand 1-Selected NSCLC
source_metadata.source_type: updated/final overall-survival analysis of an open-label randomized phase 3 trial

extraction_metadata.scope_note: The primary article and supplied supplement were inspected. Main and supplementary figures/tables were reconciled. Bibliographic entries were separated into a task queue and were not atomized. Updated high-PD-L1 and biomarker/subgroup analyses retain their exploratory status. No external current-practice verification was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.

atoms.canonical_statement: The updated IMpower110 analysis evaluated final overall survival in the high-or-intermediate and any PD-L1 expression wild-type populations and provided an updated exploratory overall-survival analysis in the high PD-L1 population.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report the primary OS analyses for the lower PD-L1 expression groups and updated exploratory results in the high PD-L1 expression group.

atoms.canonical_statement: IMpower110 was an open-label, randomized phase 3 trial comparing first-line atezolizumab with platinum-based chemotherapy.
Participants were randomized 1:1 and stratified by sex, ECOG performance status 0 versus 1, histology, and PD-L1 status.

Eligible participants had chemotherapy-naive stage IV nonsquamous or squamous NSCLC, measurable disease by RECIST 1.1, ECOG performance status 0 or 1, and tumor PD-L1 expression of at least 1% on tumor cells or tumor-infiltrating immune cells by SP142.

population.label: Eligible IMpower110 population
inclusion_criteria: Chemotherapy-naive stage IV nonsquamous or squamous NSCLC
SP142 PD-L1 expression at least 1% on tumor cells or tumor-infiltrating immune cells

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK translocations were excluded from the efficacy population for this analysis.
Atezolizumab was given at 1200 mg intravenously on day 1 of each 21-day cycle until loss of clinical benefit, unacceptable toxicity, or death.
The chemotherapy control used histology-specific platinum doublets for four or six cycles, followed by pemetrexed maintenance for nonsquamous disease or best supportive care for squamous disease.

exposures.details: Nonsquamous: cisplatin 75 mg/m2 or carboplatin AUC 6 plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 for four or six cycles, followed by pemetrexed maintenance. Squamous: cisplatin 75 mg/m2 plus gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 or carboplatin AUC 5 plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 for four or six cycles, followed by best supportive care.

atoms.canonical_statement: Protocol crossover from chemotherapy to atezolizumab was not permitted, but subsequent anticancer therapy outside the protocol was allowed.
Overall survival was the primary efficacy endpoint and was tested hierarchically across PD-L1 populations.

outcome.definition: Time-to-death endpoint used for the hierarchical primary analysis.

atoms.canonical_statement: Key secondary efficacy endpoints included progression-free survival, objective response rate, and duration of response.

concept.text: Progression-free survival, objective response rate, and duration of response

atoms.canonical_statement: Tumor assessments were scheduled every 6 weeks for 48 weeks and every 9 weeks thereafter.
Adverse events were graded with NCI CTCAE version 4.0 and coded using MedDRA version 22.1; all-cause safety included treated participants regardless of PD-L1 or EGFR/ALK status.
The statistical hierarchy tested overall survival first in the high PD-L1 group, then high-or-intermediate, then any PD-L1; failure at a level stopped formal testing at lower levels.
The final lower-PD-L1 analysis used a stratified log-rank test and Cox model; Kaplan-Meier methods estimated medians and Brookmeyer-Crowley methods estimated median confidence intervals.
A post hoc rank-preserving structural failure time sensitivity analysis adjusted chemotherapy-arm survival for subsequent non-protocol immunotherapy.
From July 2015 through February 2018, 572 patients were randomized: 285 to atezolizumab and 287 to chemotherapy.
After excluding 18 patients with sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK translocations, the any-PD-L1 wild-type efficacy population contained 554 patients, 277 per arm.

population.label: Any PD-L1 expression wild-type efficacy population

atoms.canonical_statement: The high-or-intermediate PD-L1 wild-type population contained 328 patients: 166 assigned to atezolizumab and 162 to chemotherapy.
The high PD-L1 wild-type population contained 205 patients: 107 assigned to atezolizumab and 98 to chemotherapy.
In the any-PD-L1 wild-type population, median age was 64 years with atezolizumab and 65 years with chemotherapy; 70.8% and 69.7% were male, respectively.
In the any-PD-L1 wild-type population, 65.0% of atezolizumab patients and 62.8% of chemotherapy patients had ECOG performance status 1, and about 69% in each arm had nonsquamous histology.
At the February 4, 2020 cutoff, median overall-survival follow-up was 31.3 months in the high group, 31.0 months in the high-or-intermediate group, and 30.0 months in the any-PD-L1 group.
In the high-or-intermediate PD-L1 wild-type population, median overall survival was 19.9 months with atezolizumab versus 16.1 months with chemotherapy; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.66-1.14), p=0.3091.

exposures.details: Histology-specific platinum-doublet chemotherapy followed by permitted maintenance or best supportive care as specified in the protocol.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the any-PD-L1 wild-type population, median overall survival was 18.9 months with atezolizumab versus 14.7 months with chemotherapy; HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.69-1.04). This result was not formally tested because the hierarchy stopped at the high-or-intermediate population.

atoms.canonical_statement: No new or unexpected safety signals were identified in the updated analysis.

The authors concluded that updated IMpower110 results continue to support atezolizumab monotherapy as a first-line treatment option for patients with high PD-L1 expression and wild-type EGFR/ALK NSCLC.

The authors reported no statistically significant overall-survival benefit in the high-or-intermediate PD-L1 population, and the any-PD-L1 population was not formally tested because of the hierarchical testing sequence.
The updated high-PD-L1 overall-survival analysis was exploratory because the earlier interim high-PD-L1 analysis had already crossed the prespecified efficacy boundary.
Several clinical and biomarker subgroup estimates had wide confidence intervals and small sample sizes, limiting subgroup-level inference.

F. Hoffmann-La Roche/Genentech supported the study; Genentech funded the study, provided study treatments, and collaborated on study design, data collection, analysis, and interpretation. Roche funded medical writing support.
The article reports extensive author financial relationships with pharmaceutical companies; several authors were employees of Genentech or Roche and reported company stock or equity interests.
Qualified researchers may request access to individual patient-level clinical data through the Vivli platform subject to Roche data-sharing eligibility criteria.
